title: Cost Inspector: per-unit cost breakdown, attribution flows, and pricing UI patterns
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Goal: Deliver a high-fidelity design prototype for a Console "Cost Inspector" experience that surfaces per-unit (token/request) economics, multi-dimensional attribution, and export-ready datasets while offering safe pricing UI patterns for product teams. Scope covers: (1) a Cost Inspector panel for route/model/date drill-downs; (2) an Attribution pane that slices spend by caller token, prompt family, model variant, and rollout cohort; (3) lightweight pricing controls to preview the impact of batching/quantization/caching toggles; (4) CSV/Parquet export formats with schema definitions; and (5) micro-interactions and accessibility states. This ticket covers design exploration, prototype iterations, and handoff docs for engineering and PM. Constraints: respect PII policy (no raw prompts in exports by default), ensure data table pagination for large exports, and fit within existing Console layout patterns.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Cost Inspector prototype (Figma) that supports route/model/date drilldown and per-unit breakdown at token/request granularity
Attribution pane with at least four slice dimensions and an interactive timeline for selecting windows
Pricing preview mock that simulates unit-cost deltas for batching, quantization, and cache hit-rate changes
Export modal designs for CSV and Parquet with field-level toggles and PII-safe defaults
Handoff doc with schema for export (fields, types), accessibility notes, and CSS token suggestions

engineering_notes: Export schema must support large-volume streaming; recommend Parquet for >5M rows. See GH PR with streaming uploader: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1789
Backend dependency: ENG-1987 will expose per-tag token counts. UI should support missing-data states and fallbacks.
Frontend suggestion: virtualized table (react-window) for attribution table, client-side CSV generation for small exports, server-side job for large Parquet exports.
Security: exports default to redacted_prompt=true. Provide an explicit opt-in with inline warning if a user enables raw prompt export.
ux_decisions: Use a two-tier navigation: compact inspector side-panel for quick lookups; full inspector route for deep analysis and export workflows.
Adopt 'cost facets' visual language (small cards) to show unit cost, effective cost, attribution share, and trend sparkline.
Pricing preview uses simulated knobs (batch size, quantization level, cache hit %) that recompute a projected unit cost in real-time. Changes are non-destructive and labeled as 'preview only'.
Export defaults to anonymized prompts, includes provenance fields (route, model_variant, timestamp, rollout_cohort) and a 'cost_unit' column with currency and per-token flags.
